subject: Business Studies
provisional_note: Semester 1 (Jul-Dec 2026) follows the official MoEST 2026 calendar. Semester 2 (Jan-May 2027) is inferred from the 2026 pattern and ends before the ACSEE examinations - replace it with the published 2026/2027 almanac before relying on those dates.

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of principles of business
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the principles of business
entries.learning_activity: (a) Describe the basic aspects of business environment (stakeholders in business and agents supporting business start-ups)
teaching_learning_activities: Think-ink-pair-share: Ask students to think and share business stakeholders and business agents found in their communities. Guide students to summarise their responses with regards to stakeholders and agents supporting business start-ups

Guest speaker: Invite a resourceful person to share with students on his or her experience based on: Stakeholders in business and Agents supporting business start-ups. Then, summarise what they have learnt from the resourceful person

Skills lab: Guide students to formulate a business club. Provide students with the business club guidelines and milestones. Ask them to work on components of the simple constitution of a club such as membership, leadership, finance, disputes, dissolution and share
entries.assessment: Business environment clearly described
resources: Online/offline sources and bronchers from Tanzania National Business Council (TNBC) and Tanzania Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculiture (TCCIA)
entries.references: TIE, Business Studies for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of principles of business
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the principles of business
entries.learning_activity: (b) Describe some advanced aspects of the business units (size classification, company and company’ s management, franchise, joint ventures and cooperatives, formation and dissolution)
teaching_learning_activities: Role play: Use manageable groups to role play features associated with running a business as a group
Relate the role play to the meaning, features, formation and dissolution of company, franchise, joint venture, and cooperatives

Case study: Provide case studies that portray company, franchise, joint venture and cooperative businesses. In manageable groups, students should be assigned one of the cases to discuss and share lessons learnt from the case study to the whole class
Skills lab: Guide students in manageable groups, to develop a Memorandum and Articles of Association using a template provided to them
Let students present their draft of the Memorandum and Articles of Association to receive feedback for further improvement
Project activity: Students polish the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
entries.assessment: Some advanced aspects of the business units clearly described
resources: Company Act, videos/ trade shows, Online/offline sources
entries.references: TIE, Business Studies for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of principles of business
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the principles of business
entries.learning_activity: (c) Describe some advanced aspects of financing medium businesses (internal and external sources: retained earnings, sale and leaseback of non-current assets, share capital, venture capital, overdrafts, loans, debentures, crowd funding and government grants)
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Organise students in manageable groups to reflect and share on the sources of business financing. Relate students’ reflections to the internal and external sources of business financing
Gamification: Use game design techniques to present scenarios that will require students to organise finance for business start-ups from among themselves
Case study: Organise students in manageable groups and provide a case study that portrays internal and external sources of financing. Let students discuss and share lessons learnt from the case study
Guest speaker: Invite a resourceful person who can share with the students on advanced aspects of financing businesses. Let students summarise what they have learnt in relation to sources of finance
entries.assessment: Some advanced aspects of financing medium businesses clearly described
resources: Loan application forms, and Online/offline sources
entries.references: TIE, Business Studies for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate an understanding of the business environment
entries.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the policies and laws governing medium scale business
entries.learning_activity: (a) Explore the basic aspects of the policy and regulatory environment governing medium businesses in Tanzania (roles of government and non-governmental agencies, policies, laws and by-laws)
teaching_learning_activities: Field trip: Guide students to visit nearest regulatory authority and find out policies governing medium businesses in Tanzania

Group activity: Organise students in manageable groups to discuss the roles of government and non-governmental agencies, policies, laws and by-laws learned in a field trip and write a short report that summarises the lessons

Guest speaker: Invite resourceful person from government agencies responsible for regulating medium business operations in Tanzania and share the following: (i) Government and non - government agencies; (ii) roles of such agencies; and (iii) Business regulations (laws, policies, by-laws) by writing and submitting a report with recommendations on how they will comply with business regulations in their business club
entries.assessment: Basic aspects of the policy and regulatory environment governing medium sized businesses in Tanzania are effectively explored
resources: Online/offline sources, Rules, regulations and policies governing business in Tanzania
entries.references: TIE, Business Studies for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate an understanding of the business environment
entries.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the policies and laws governing medium scale business
entries.learning_activity: (b) Describe procedures for registering medium businesses in Tanzania (types of licences, importance of registration and sanctions for non-compliance)
teaching_learning_activities: Reflection: Guide students to use quiz trivia to recall the importance of business compliance and certification. Relate their responses to types of licences, importance of registration and certification and compliance

Guest speaker: Invite a staff working at district/agency who is in charge of supervising businesses registration and licensing in the community. The resource person should share his/her experience on; procedure for registration and licensing a medium businesses and penalties for non-compliance
Skills lab: Using a template of a business registration guide, students in manageable groups discuss the steps for registering businesses with relevant authorities

Project activity: Task students in manageable groups to prepare the procedures of registering a medium business of their choice, then discuss or foresee the registration challenges they may encounter and the mitigation plan of the identified challenges
entries.assessment: Procedures for registering medium sized businesses in Tanzania is clearly described
resources: Procedures guide book for registration, and Sample of application form for registration, Company Act, The Business Activities Registration Act, Business registration guide book, Online/offline sources
entries.references: TIE, Business Studies for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education
